ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sound is whispered, with no buzz in the throat? (1 mark)
   A. /v/
   B. /f/
   C. /g/
   D. /d/

2. In the family tree in the lesson, Amina's father's sister is her (1 mark)
   A. grandmother
   B. aunt
   C. sibling
   D. cousin

3. What are guide words? (1 mark)
   A. Words that rhyme
   B. The longest words in the book
   C. The first and last words on a dictionary page
   D. The words on the cover

4. Which is the best first step to look up the word 'orphan'? (1 mark)
   A. Read every page
   B. Ask a friend to spell it
   C. Open at the letter z
   D. Open the dictionary at the letter o

5. Why should you check your form before handing it in? (1 mark)
   A. To find missing or wrong information
   B. To hide it
   C. To make it dirty
   D. To lose it

6. If you make a small mistake on a form, you should (1 mark)
   A. scribble over it
   B. tear the page
   C. leave it
   D. draw one neat line through it and write the correct word

7. Which of these words has /r/ as its first sound? (1 mark)
   A. load
   B. ribbon
   C. light
   D. lake

8. What should you do before you read a story? (1 mark)
   A. Read the last page only
   B. Write the answers
   C. Close the book
   D. Read the title and look at the pictures

9. What is the plural of 'church'? (1 mark)
   A. churchen
   B. churchies
   C. churches
   D. churchs

10. Plural nouns: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. The woman are selling tomatoes.
   B. The women are selling tomatoes.
   C. The womans are selling tomatoes.
   D. The women is selling tomatoes.

11. Which is the best way to end a story? (1 mark)
   A. With a feeling or a lesson
   B. With nothing
   C. With a list of numbers
   D. With the word 'the'

12. 'The sun was as warm as a fresh loaf of bread.' This sentence uses (1 mark)
   A. a question
   B. a command
   C. a list
   D. a simile

13. Which is a greeting for the afternoon? (1 mark)
   A. Good night
   B. Good afternoon
   C. Good morning
   D. Good luck

14. Which word best describes Neema in the passage? (1 mark)
   A. greedy
   B. rude
   C. lazy
   D. honest

15. Complete: 'Mother bought enough flour ___ chapati.' (1 mark)
   A. by make
   B. for make
   C. to make
   D. making

16. Which letter is a tall letter? (1 mark)
   A. e
   B. a
   C. n
   D. h

17. In the word 'emergency', which syllable is stressed? (1 mark)
   A. The fourth
   B. The third
   C. The first
   D. The second

18. Which pronoun replaces 'Ali and I'? (1 mark)
   A. we
   B. you
   C. they
   D. he

19. Where does the sender's address go in a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. In the middle
   B. At the top right
   C. After the name
   D. At the bottom left

20. Which is a minimal pair for /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. book, look
   B. jam, ham
   C. pen, pin
   D. safe, save

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how a word wheel can help you make new words. Give an example with the ending -oy. (4 marks)

22. Describe how you would set up a reading club in your class. (4 marks)

23. Write two words with the sound /uː/ and two words with /ʊ/. (2 marks)

24. Explain why it is important to put the stress on the right syllable. (2 marks)

25. Give two examples of regular plurals and two of irregular plurals. (2 marks)

26. Read: 'Juma asked his mother to add vegetables to his lunch.' Say why Juma did this, using the story 'A Pot of Vegetables'. (2 marks)

27. Write a or an before each word: egg, banana, umbrella, hour. (2 marks)

28. List the three main parts of a composition and say what each does. (3 marks)

29. Correct these sentences: (a) 'I have money enough to buy bread.' (b) 'She has alot of friends.' (2 marks)

30. Replace the second mention with a pronoun: 'Neema saw the bridge. Neema liked the bridge.' (2 marks)

31. Why is it important to interpret road signs correctly? (2 marks)

32. Rewrite in the plural: 'The child put a loaf and a tomato in the box.' (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — /f/
   /f/ is a whispered sound. /v/, /d/ and /g/ are voiced.

2. B — aunt
   A father's sister is an aunt.

3. C — The first and last words on a dictionary page
   They show which words can be found on the page.

4. D — Open the dictionary at the letter o
   Words are in alphabetical order, so start with the first letter.

5. A — To find missing or wrong information
   Checking finds mistakes that can cause problems later.

6. D — draw one neat line through it and write the correct word
   A neat single line keeps the form readable.

7. B — ribbon
   Ribbon starts with /r/.

8. D — Read the title and look at the pictures
   The title and pictures help you predict.

9. C — churches
   Nouns ending in ch add es.

10. B — The women are selling tomatoes.
   Women is plural and takes are.

11. A — With a feeling or a lesson
   A good ending gives the reader a feeling or a message.

12. D — a simile
   It compares the sun to bread using as ... as.

13. B — Good afternoon
   Good afternoon is used after midday.

14. D — honest
   She returned the purse and refused a reward.

15. C — to make
   Use to + verb.

16. D — h
   H reaches the top line.

17. D — The second
   We say e-MER-gen-cy.

18. A — we
   We includes the speaker and another person.

19. B — At the top right
   Address and date are at the top right.

20. D — safe, save
   They differ in the last sound.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: A word wheel has a fixed ending and different beginning letters. You change the first letter to make a new word. With -oy you can make boy, toy and joy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixed ending, 1 mark for changing the first letter, 1 mark each for two correct words.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a day, time and place; give members roles; agree on rules such as taking turns; and read silently then share what was read.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: /uː/: food, spoon. /ʊ/: book, cook.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Wrong stress can make a word hard to understand, and it can change the word from a noun to a verb.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Regular: books, dishes. Irregular: men, feet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mama Zuri told him vegetables give vitamins that protect the body from sickness, so he wanted to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for vitamins or protection and 1 mark for linking to Juma.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: an egg, a banana, an umbrella, an hour
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each correct answer.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Introduction: tells who, where and when. Body: tells what happened in order. Conclusion: tells how it ended or how the writer felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part with its job.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) I have enough money to buy bread. (b) She has a lot of friends.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema saw the bridge. She liked it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for she and 1 mark for it.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Signs warn us of danger and tell us what to do, so misunderstanding one could cause an accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what signs do and 1 mark for the danger of misunderstanding.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: The children put loaves and tomatoes in the boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for children, loaves and tomatoes and boxes (award 3 for all correct).
